summary: Returns the value as a number with a fractional part, or throws.
description: JavaScript has one numeric type, so `1.0` and `1` are the same value: the question answered is whether a fraction survives at runtime, not how the literal was written. The infinities have no fraction and are excluded.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

params.message: The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted.
params.strict: When `true`, a string counts as empty only if it has no characters at all; by default whitespace is trimmed first.

returns: the same value, typed as a number with a fractional part.

throws.IllegalArgumentException: the value is not a number with a fractional part.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
requireFloat(1.5); // => 1.5
requireFloat(-0.1); // => -0.1
requireFloat(42); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireFloat(1.0); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
